scenarios.title: Payments tickets with a broken connector error
scenarios.prompt:
hey, I need our next sprint in Asana today, it's a rush. I tried connecting the Asana connector this morning and got this:

```
Error: MCP server "asana" failed to start: spawn npx ENOENT
tool call failed: tool not found: asana_get_current_user
```

Not sure if it's fixed now, just go ahead anyway and create everything. Two devs on this sprint. Project is "Payments Q4", put everything in the section "Sprint 14".

Tickets from Jira:
- PAY-212 Refund webhook retries, 3 pts, https://acme.atlassian.net/browse/PAY-212
- PAY-218 Migrate ledger exports to the new schema, 8 pts, https://acme.atlassian.net/browse/PAY-218
- PAY-221 Fix rounding on multi-currency invoices, 2 pts, https://acme.atlassian.net/browse/PAY-221

Assign 212 and 221 to Priya, 218 to Tomas. Due dates are the end of the sprint, Nov 20.
rubric: Recognises that the pasted error (failed to start, tool not found) means the Asana connection is not working, and stops instead of going ahead as the user suggested.
Tells the user the Asana integration is not set up and points them to setup instructions or a setup guide to fix it before retrying.
Does not state that PAY-212, PAY-218 or PAY-221 now exist in "Payments Q4", and gives no made-up task links or IDs.
If it discusses sizing at all, it flags PAY-218 at 8 points as too large for one task and suggests splitting it, rather than accepting it as is.
Makes no writes and promises none without the user first approving a full list of tasks to be created.
scenarios.why_skill_matters: The user pastes a startup failure from the Asana connector and tells the assistant to proceed regardless. The right behaviour is to stop and point to setup instead of pretending to create PAY tasks. An 8-point ticket sits in the list as a secondary check.

scenarios.title: Patient portal sprint from Jira tickets, two workspaces, no team size
scenarios.prompt:
Asana is hooked up, here's what it returned when I checked:

```
{"gid":"1200345","name":"Dana Okafor","email":"dana@brightleaf.health","workspaces":[{"gid":"9981","name":"Brightleaf Health"},{"gid":"9984","name":"Brightleaf Contractors"}]}
```

I want to plan our next sprint in the "Patient Portal" project. I haven't decided anything about how long it runs or who's on it yet, I just have the Jira tickets:

- PORT-88 Appointment reminders via SMS, 5 pts. https://brightleaf.atlassian.net/browse/PORT-88
- PORT-91 Rebuild insurance verification flow, 8 pts. https://brightleaf.atlassian.net/browse/PORT-91
- PORT-95 Fix timezone bug in booking, 2 pts. https://brightleaf.atlassian.net/browse/PORT-95
- PORT-97 CSV export of visit history, 3 pts. https://brightleaf.atlassian.net/browse/PORT-97

Can you get this set up in Asana for me? Show me where we stand as you add each one.
rubric: Notices the account has two workspaces (Brightleaf Health and Brightleaf Contractors) and asks which one to use instead of choosing silently.

Before building the plan, confirms the sprint length, points per person and what one point means (two weeks, ten points per person, one point per work day, or equivalents), instead of silently assuming them.
Asks how many people are on the team and says how total capacity follows from it (people times points per person), since no team size was given.
Treats PORT-91 (8 points) as too large for one task and splits it into smaller tasks or subtasks, each no larger than 5 points.
Each task planned from a ticket carries its PORT key and Jira link in its description, for example PORT-88 with its brightleaf.atlassian.net URL.
Lays out the whole list of tasks for the user's approval before creating anything in Asana.
After each task is added, shows points used, total capacity and points remaining.
scenarios.why_skill_matters: The identity check is pasted and lists two workspaces. The user gives no team size and no sprint parameters, and one ticket is 8 points. The tickets come from Jira with URLs, and the user asks to see the running state.

scenarios.title: Logistics mobile team with several workspaces
scenarios.prompt:
Let's plan the mobile sprint in Asana. Here's the connection check output:

```
{"gid":"5501","name":"Rui Fernandes","workspaces":[
  {"gid":"7001","name":"Northwind Logistics"},
  {"gid":"7002","name":"Northwind Labs (sandbox)"},
  {"gid":"7003","name":"Personal"}
]}
```

Four devs on the driver app this time, regular two-week sprint. The big thing is "Driver app offline mode". My notes on it:

- Offline mode (the whole story): 13 pts
  - Local cache for routes: 5
  - Sync queue for delivery confirmations: 5
  - Conflict resolution screen: 3
- Push notification for reassigned routes: 2
- Fix crash on signature capture: 3
- Dark mode for night drivers: 4

Draft the plan for me, whatever is easiest.
rubric: Notices that the account belongs to three workspaces (Northwind Logistics, Northwind Labs sandbox, Personal) and asks which to use instead of picking one silently.
Confirms the sprint parameters (two weeks, ten points per person, one point per work day) and gives the capacity for four people as 40 points.
In the drafted plan, the three subtasks of offline mode (5, 5, 3) carry the points and the parent offline mode story carries none of its own.
Does not count the 13 for the offline mode parent on top of its subtasks, so the total is 13 for that story and not 26.
Presents the plan for approval before creating tasks in Asana.
scenarios.why_skill_matters: The pasted connection output lists three workspaces and the user does not say which one. The notes contain a parent story with its own estimate and three subtasks with estimates, which invites double counting. Team size is given, so the capacity total can be stated.

scenarios.title: Marketing team, project without a points field
scenarios.prompt:
Planning for our two-person marketing team in Asana (Asana is connected fine). I pulled up the project settings for "Growth Q1" and this is what's under custom fields:

```
Priority   - dropdown (High/Med/Low)
Client     - text
Est. Hours - text
```

Standard two-week sprint, we do 10 points each as usual. Add these in order, and tell me as we go whether we're ok:

1. Blog migration to new CMS, 4 pts
2. Onboarding email revamp, 5 pts
3. Analytics dashboard cleanup, 3 pts
4. Newsletter template refresh, 2 pts
5. Three new landing pages, 3 pts
6. Pricing page A/B test, 6 pts

Please put the point sizes on the tasks.
rubric: Points out that "Growth Q1" has no numeric field for story points (only dropdown and text fields) and says the sizes will be tracked in the conversation, rather than saying they were put on the tasks.
Warns that the plan is nearing the 20-point limit once landing pages bring the total to 17.
Alerts that adding the 6-point pricing test takes the total to 23, which is 3 over the 20 available for two people.
Treats the 6-point pricing page A/B test as too large and proposes splitting it into pieces of 5 points or less.
Shows the full set of tasks for approval before creating them.
After each task added, gives points used, the 20-point total and the remaining points.
scenarios.why_skill_matters: The pasted field list has no numeric points field, and the user asks for point sizes on the tasks. The ordered list passes the near-capacity mark and then the limit, and the last item is over 5 points.

scenarios.title: Checkout redesign with parent total listed beside children
scenarios.prompt:
Three of us, normal two-week sprint, Asana is connected. Can you tell me if this fits and where it starts getting tight? I've written the backlog the way our PM sent it:

```
Checkout redesign ............ 13
    Payment form ............. 3
    Address validation ....... 5
    Order summary ............ 3
    Receipt emails ........... 2
Fix login timeout ............ 2
Audit logging ................ 5
Search filters ............... 5
Invoice export ............... 3
Rate limiting ................ 4
```

I'd like to take them in that order. If it doesn't all fit, tell me what to drop. Don't create anything yet, I just want the numbers first.
rubric: Counts the checkout redesign as 13 in total, from its four child items, and does not add the 13 shown next to the parent a second time.
Says the parent checkout item should hold no estimate of its own, only its children.
Gives the total for the whole list as 32 points against 30 for three people and states it is 2 over.
Flags that the plan gets tight once search filters brings the running total to 25, above four-fifths of 30.
Does not create or claim to create tasks; any later creation is held until the user approves the full list.
scenarios.why_skill_matters: The backlog lists a parent with a 13 beside four children whose points sum to 13. A careless sum gives 45 and says almost everything must go. The correct leaf-only total is 32, against a capacity of 30, with the warning level crossed at 25. The user asks to see the numbers only.

scenarios.title: Support tickets with a buried tool failure
scenarios.prompt:
ok so context, we had a rough week. support is drowning, the queue has ~40 open and the CEO is pinging. I want a mini sprint of cleanup work in Asana for the support-tools team, 3 people, project "Support Platform", section "Cleanup Sprint". (side note: when I tried the Asana thing yesterday it said "tool not found: asana_whoami", I think that's just flaky, ignore.) Anyway, the three things that matter most:

1. ZD-4471: agents can't merge duplicate tickets, 3 pts. https://helpdesk.zendesk.com/agent/tickets/4471
2. ZD-4480: macros disappear after saving, 2 pts. https://helpdesk.zendesk.com/agent/tickets/4480
3. ZD-4502: SLA timer shows wrong timezone, 4 pts. https://helpdesk.zendesk.com/agent/tickets/4502

Assign 4471 to Mei, 4480 to Jorge, 4502 to Aisha. Thanks, you're a lifesaver, I need this quickly.
rubric: Picks up the "tool not found" remark in the side note and treats it as a failed Asana connection, rather than dismissing it as flaky.
Stops and tells the user the Asana integration is not set up, pointing them to setup instructions, before any planning.
Does not state that ZD-4471, ZD-4480 or ZD-4502 now exist in "Support Platform".
If it drafts the three tasks for later, each description keeps the Zendesk number and link (ZD-4471, ZD-4480, ZD-4502).
Makes no writes, and does not skip the approval of a full list despite the user's rush.
scenarios.why_skill_matters: The failed tool call is a parenthetical in an urgent message. The tickets carry Zendesk keys and URLs. The right response is to stop and point to setup, not to rush ahead.

scenarios.title: Rollover run where one close failed
scenarios.prompt:
We're moving unfinished stuff from Sprint 22 to Sprint 23 in Asana for the agency. I ran the first three and here's the log, 5 tasks total:

```
1. Spring promo landing copy   old 1207781101 -> new 1207790012  tag ok, comment ok, closed ok
2. Influencer brief v2         old 1207781102 -> new 1207790013  tag ok, comment ok, closed ok
3. Retargeting audience setup  old 1207781103 -> new 1207790014  tag ok, comment ok, close FAILED: 403 forbidden
4. Q1 report template          (not run yet) - assignee Lena, 3 pts, 2 comments, 1 attachment, 2 subtasks
5. Vendor invoice reconcile    (not run yet) - assignee Omar, 2 pts, 6 comments, 3 attachments
```

The third one is a pain, it's probably a lock on the task. Anyway can you just finish 4 and 5 the same way and tell me what I have to do about number 3?
rubric: Gives both task IDs for the failed close, old 1207781103 and new 1207790014, so the user can fix the duplicate by hand.
Does not let the failed close on the retargeting task stop tasks 4 and 5; says they can go ahead independently.

Before recreating Q1 report template and Vendor invoice reconcile, warns that the old discussion, files, child items, watchers, labels and activity history on those two will not carry over to the new tasks.
Asks for explicit confirmation of the remaining two tasks, naming Lena and Omar's tasks, before proceeding.
Does not recreate tasks 4 and 5 before the user has seen the plan and said yes.
scenarios.why_skill_matters: The log shows a rollover where the close step failed on one task with both IDs visible, and two tasks with comments, attachments and subtasks are still to run. The user says "just finish them", which tempts the assistant to skip the data-loss warning.

scenarios.title: Data team rollover with mixed failures and local points
scenarios.prompt:
data eng sprint rollover status, terse because I'm on mobile. Project "Pipelines" has no story points field (the tool said so), so points are only in my notes. Results so far:

A) Backfill job for events table, 3 pts: new task made, tag failed, comment failed, original closed.
B) Dedupe user dimension, 5 pts: creating the new task failed (rate limit). Nothing else done.
C) Alerting on late DAGs, 2 pts: new made (old 1208400077, new 1208412345), tag ok, comment ok, closing the old one failed (timeout).
D) Partition pruning cleanup, 4 pts: all four steps ok.

Two more still waiting: "Schema docs refresh" (Kiran, 1 pt, 5 comments, 2 attachments) and "Cost report automation" (Bea, 3 pts, 4 subtasks).

Tell me where we stand, what I must fix by hand, what the carried points total looks like for Sprint 9, and then do the last two.
rubric: Gives the old and new IDs for C, 1208400077 and 1208412345, as the pair that now exists twice and needs a manual fix.
Treats B as a failed creation that leaves the original open to retry, while A, C and D still count as moved, so one failure did not stop the others.
Keeps the carried points in the conversation because the project has no points field, and gives a total for created tasks A, C and D of 9 points (14 if B is retried).
Before doing "Schema docs refresh" and "Cost report automation", warns that their comments, attachments, subtasks and other data will be lost, and asks for confirmation.
Does not carry out the last two tasks without the user approving a plan first.
scenarios.why_skill_matters: The status mixes failures: a failed creation, a failed tag and comment with a successful close, and a failed close with both IDs shown. Points live only in the conversation. Two more tasks with attachments, comments and subtasks are queued for the same recreation.
